title: tenable_sc_credential data block
description: The `data` block of a `tenable_sc_credential` secret, read by the Tenable collector and the observation command (req-tenable-connection). Write one envelope for each Tenable Security Center instance. The connection settings, the scope filter and the API keys sit together in one operator-owned file, so nobody who can edit a grid node can point the keys at another host or narrow what is read. The tenable plugin owns this schema and checks it before any request. Use a Security Center user with a READ-ONLY role, limited to the repositories that should be read. Its API keys need Security Center 5.13 or later. One instance must not span several networks: `network_name` is trusted as written and the plugin cannot detect a wrong one (accepted for v0, 2026-11-12). Strict: every field is described, and fields not listed here are refused.

base_url.description: The Security Center root, for example https://sc.example:443. Both http and https are accepted as written, and the client never changes the scheme. A plain http root sends the keys and every response unencrypted, and every run that uses one records PLAINTEXT_TRANSPORT. Refused: userinfo, a query, a fragment, port 0, a host ending in a dot, and a path with empty, dot or percent-encoded segments. Host and scheme are lower-cased and the port is made explicit, so one instance has one key however its URL is spelled.

access_key.description: The API access key of a Security Center user with API-key authentication enabled, sent in the X-APIKey header. Never printed, logged, stored on a node or placed in a URL.

secret_key.description: The API secret key that pairs with access_key. Never printed, logged, stored on a node or placed in a URL.

ssl_verify.description: Whether to verify the instance's TLS certificate. Defaults to true, and the client always passes the value explicitly, so pyTenable's own default of false is never reached. false is honoured because the operator knows the network, and every run that applies it records TLS_VERIFICATION_DISABLED.

ca_bundle.description: The absolute path of a PEM file on the host holding the CA certificates to trust for this instance, for a private CA. Give the path, never the file's contents. Ignored when ssl_verify is false.

network_name.description: The network this instance's results come from, as a value of computing_core's tap.computing.network_name dimension (for example corp, or Internet for public addresses). It names where the results were gathered, not where the scanner sits. Every address and port fact from this instance is written on this network, and it is recorded on the Security Center node.

scope.description: The server-side filter that narrows what each run reads (req-tenable-scope). Leave it out to read everything the credential can see. Each option is a scope filter, a non-resolving filter or a window filter, and only a run that uses scope filters alone, or none, resolves findings by absence. Every run records the filter exactly as applied. A saved Security Center query is not supported.

repository_ids.description: Scope filter: read only these repository ids (Security Center's repositoryIDs filter).

asset_ids.description: Non-resolving filter: read only results on hosts in these asset lists (Security Center's asset filter). Membership lives in Security Center, so a run that uses it resolves nothing by absence.

min_severity.description: Non-resolving filter: read only results at or above this severity, from 0 (informational) to 4 (critical). Leave it out to collect informational results too.

plugin_ids.description: Scope filter: read only results from these plugin ids.

plugin_families.description: Non-resolving filter: read only results from plugins in these family ids. A plugin's family can change while its results keep their keys.

exclude_plugin_ids.description: Scope filter: leave out results from these plugin ids. Applied by the collector after the read unless an observation shows Security Center supports excluding them on the server.

ports.description: Scope filter: read only results on these ports, given as strings because Security Center reports ports as strings.

protocols.description: Scope filter: read only results on these protocols, as Security Center names them (for example TCP, UDP, ICMP).

exploit_available.description: Non-resolving filter: read only results whose plugin has a known exploit (true) or none (false).

has_cve.description: Non-resolving filter: read only results whose plugin names a CVE.

recast_risk_status.description: Non-resolving filter: read only recast results (recast) or results that were not recast (notRecast). There is no accepted-risk option: every read asks for accepted and non-accepted results alike (req-tenable-transport-9), so accepting a risk in Tenable never looks like a fix.

last_seen_within.description: Window filter: read only results last seen within this many days. Results that are still open fall outside the window, so a run that uses it resolves nothing by absence.

max_records.description: Safety ceiling: the most records read for each repository and view. A read that reaches it is recorded as possibly truncated and resolves nothing in that repository.

scan_result_window_days.description: How many days back the scan-result list is read, by finish time (req-tenable-scan-result). Defaults to 30.

feed_stale_days.description: How many days old the plugin feed may be before a run records FEED_STALE (req-tenable-probe-5). Defaults to 7.
